precedence_source.note: Order the payer reports when a claim breaks several rules. Learned from history claims that break two or more rules (python -m claimcheck.precedence; evidence in rules/precedence_evidence.json). No pair was seen both ways. Unlike Northwind and Harbor, Summit reports authorization problems (D07, D08) ahead of D09. D05 vs D02/D03 was never observed and is placed last by analogy with Northwind.

source.quote: Summit requires a verified EVV record for each billed date of service, member and service
partial units are not billable, and units above verified time will be denied
A Summit authorization number is mandatory on every claim
The authorization must be for the member and service billed and cover the date of service
claims exceeding the balance will be denied
Claims must be received within 60 calendar days of the date of service

source.ref: PY03_summit_provider_manual.md 9.5 (contract terms not published) + payer remarks 'Contract amendment 3: services must be billed in whole hours'
source.quote: Units not billable per amendment 3 (hourly increments)
source.evidence: Summit claims for a number of units that is not a multiple of 4: every one with a date of service up to 2026-06-30 that broke no other rule was paid; every one from 2026-07-01 was denied (D10, or D99 with the same remark). The cut-off follows the date of service, not the submission date: a June claim submitted on 2026-08-19 was paid.
